task_name: NIGHTFORM - Low Beam music release package
client_brief:
Low Beam is the next NIGHTFORM release. We need a teaser, an upright cut and cover artwork that feel like one release. Let the picture respond to the actual track, including how the excerpt arrives and finishes; a random music bed will not do. Keep the artist and release information accurate and the atmosphere controlled. The cleared track excerpt must be supplied before the edit begins. Any new supporting footage must follow the same approved visual direction rather than replacing the performer with a different person.

The commission

 Low Beam release teaser: 1 named export. The picture rhythm responds to the supplied track. The excerpt ends on a coherent musical phrase. The release details are accurate.

 Music release vertical cut: 1 named export. The performer remains recognisable. The release action is readable.

 Music release cover: 1 named export. The artist and track names are correct.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. Speech-led work requires supplied or explicitly authorised synthetic speech; do not invent documentary speech.
- Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live-action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Self released independent electronic music. Streaming first, with physical vinyl and cassette editions through independent record shops.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A solo project running since 2020 in Portland, Oregon. One artist who writes, produces and releases everything without a label.
brand_identity.about: NIGHTFORM is a self released electronic project built on mood: late, atmospheric, cinematic tracks that sound like driving at night. The next single, Low Beam, is bought on feeling and on the sense that one person made the whole thing, so every visual has to carry the same nocturnal weight as the music.
brand_identity.audience: Streaming listeners roughly nineteen to thirty four who follow the mood. Physical buyers pay twelve to twenty eight dollars for vinyl and cassette through independent shops.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent, no label, priced as a self released record. The look has to be dark, grainy and slightly rough, never bright, clean and commercial, which would read as a car advert or a stock reel. Total blackness is the other failure: the road still has to be legible on a phone in daylight.
brand_identity.typography: A clean geometric or grotesque sans set tight and quiet, letting the imagery carry the mood. Captions and the artist name stay legible over dark moving frames at arm's length. No script, no ornament, no filmic distress on the letterforms.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and evocative, closer to a liner note than a sales line. Example line the brand would write: "Low Beam. Recorded from the passenger seat, north of the city, around eleven at night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark survives only as a flat exported picture: separated white capitals on a solid black square, from a source file no one still has. It has to be recovered as usable artwork. The previous release's sleeve card exists only as the printer's press PDF, and the whole visual identity for this single comes out of one forty five second night take.
brand_identity.values: One person, one mood, made without a label. The artist changes the words up to the drop date and cannot re commission, so anything text bearing has to stay editable.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
